title: Key-value, document or wide-column?

rows.label: In one line
values: A value under a key
A JSON document the database can look inside
Partitions of rows, kept sorted, built for heavy writes

rows.label: What the database sees
values: A key and a value it never parses
Every field, including nested objects and arrays
Rows with a partition key, clustering columns and other columns

rows.label: How you read
values: Get by key; some add ranges (DynamoDB sort keys) or data structures (Redis lists, sets, counters)
Filter, sort and aggregate on any field; fetch by ID
One partition, or a sorted slice of it; little else without another table

rows.label: Secondary indexes
values: Usually none; DynamoDB has global secondary indexes
On any field, including nested ones and arrays
Limited: Cassandra has Storage Attached Indexes since 5.0; Bigtable indexes only the row key

rows.label: Schema
values: None
Per document, with optional validation
Declared columns in CQL; just column families in Bigtable and HBase

rows.label: Updates
values: Replace the whole value, or atomic operations like `INCR`
Change single fields in place with operators like `$set`
Write individual columns; every write is appended, and deletes leave tombstones

rows.label: How it scales
values: Hash the key across partitions
Shard by a chosen key; queries without it go to every shard
Partitions spread by hash or key range, with replicas that take writes

rows.label: Reach for it for
values: Sessions, carts, counters, feature flags, cluster configuration
Product catalogs, user profiles, content
Time series, event logs, messaging, IoT

rows.label: Examples
values: Valkey, Redis, DynamoDB, etcd
MongoDB, Firestore, DocumentDB, Cosmos DB
Cassandra, ScyllaDB, Bigtable, HBase, Keyspaces

tip: All three hash or range-split a key to spread data across machines, which is why they get lumped together as NoSQL. The difference is how much of your data the database understands. If you only ever fetch by ID, a key-value store is enough; if you search by fields inside records, use documents; if you write a lot and read back ranges within a partition, use wide-column. Some products span two: DynamoDB is both key-value and document, and Redis has a JSON type.
